subject: history
topicDisplay: World History Topic: Causes & Effects of 20th-Century Wars
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A key long-term cause of the First World War was:
questions.explain: The Triple Alliance and Triple Entente drew powers into conflict; MAIN factors are standard causes.

questions.q: The immediate trigger of the First World War (1914) was:
options: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
questions.explain: The assassination in Sarajevo triggered the July Crisis and the outbreak of war.

questions.q: The acronym MAIN for the causes of WWI stands for militarism, alliances, imperialism and:
questions.explain: Militarism, Alliances, Imperialism and Nationalism are commonly cited long-term causes of WWI.

questions.q: The Second World War in Europe began in September 1939 when Germany invaded:
questions.explain: Germany's invasion of Poland led Britain and France to declare war.

questions.q: The policy of appeasement (e.g. the Munich Agreement 1938) involved:
options: Making concessions to an aggressor to avoid war
questions.explain: Appeasement gave concessions (e.g. the Sudetenland) hoping to prevent a wider war.

questions.q: The Treaty of Versailles (1919) is often argued to be a cause of WWII because it:
questions.explain: Harsh terms and reparations fuelled grievance exploited by the Nazis.

questions.q: 'Total war' refers to:
options: Mobilising a society's entire population and economy for war
A war fought only by professional soldiers
A war with no civilian impact
questions.explain: Total war harnesses the whole economy and society, blurring the line between soldiers and civilians.

questions.q: The Second World War in the Pacific ended in 1945 after:
options: The atomic bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
The fall of the Berlin Wall
questions.explain: Japan surrendered following the atomic bombings and Soviet entry into the Pacific war.

questions.q: The Spanish Civil War (1936-39) was won by:
questions.explain: Franco's Nationalists, aided by Germany and Italy, defeated the Republicans.

questions.q: Technological developments changed 20th-century warfare, for example through:
options: Aircraft, tanks and later nuclear weapons
questions.explain: New technologies transformed the scale and nature of warfare across the century.

questions.q: A major political effect of the First World War was:
options: The collapse of empires (Austro-Hungarian, Ottoman, Russian)
The founding of the Roman Empire
questions.explain: WWI led to the fall of several empires and the redrawing of borders.

questions.q: The League of Nations was established after WWI to:
questions.explain: The League aimed to prevent war via collective security, though it ultimately proved weak.

questions.q: A social effect of the world wars was:
options: A changing role for women, including wartime employment
A decline in industrial production forever
questions.explain: Wartime demands drew many women into the workforce, with lasting social effects.

questions.q: After WWII, US aid to help rebuild Western Europe was known as the:
questions.explain: The Marshall Plan provided US economic aid to rebuild and stabilise Western Europe.

questions.q: Distinguishing long-term, short-term and immediate causes of a war is an example of the historical concept of:
questions.explain: Analysing different types of causes is central to the concept of causation.

questions.q: Guerrilla warfare involves:
options: Irregular tactics by small, mobile groups
questions.explain: Guerrilla tactics use mobility, ambush and irregular forces, common in 20th-century conflicts.

questions.q: Nationalism contributed to 20th-century wars by:
options: Encouraging rivalry, expansion and ethnic tension
questions.explain: Aggressive nationalism drove territorial ambitions and rivalries that led to war.

questions.q: The Chinese Civil War resumed after 1945 between the Communists (Mao) and the:
questions.explain: The CCP and GMD resumed civil war after WWII, ending in Communist victory in 1949.

questions.q: A historian weighing whether the Treaty of Versailles or the Great Depression was more important in causing WWII is assessing:
options: The relative importance of different causes
questions.explain: Comparing the weight of causes is a core analytical skill in evaluating causation.

questions.q: The 'home front' in total war refers to:
options: Civilian society mobilised to support the war effort
questions.explain: The home front involved rationing, war production and civilian contributions to the war effort.
